answer: To pay agents that wander through a grove mapping opal deposits, assign survey slots using a lottery over locked credits. Each credit gets one ticket, with no extra ticket for a new key; deposits stay locked for the survey period and cannot enter overlapping draws. Splitting 100 credits among 100 aliases gives the same total odds as one 100-credit account. Capturing more slots requires tying up additional funds and bearing their financing cost. This depends on an unpredictable draw and a shared ledger that enforces every deposit lock.
